tool.name: attack_surface_intel
tool.description:
Look up Shodan + Censys attack-surface intelligence for a domain or IP target. Surfaces the attacker's-view of the asset's internet exposure: open ports, service banners, software versions, historical scan timestamps, and CVE matches. Complements `reverse_ip_discovery` (#23) and `domain_reputation` (#63) with operational intelligence.
| Source | Auth | API | Free tier | |---|---|---|---| | **Shodan** | `STRIX_SHODAN_KEY` | `GET https://api.shodan.io/shodan/host/?key=...` | 100 queries/month | | **Censys** | `STRIX_CENSYS_API_ID` + `STRIX_CENSYS_API_SECRET` | `GET https://search.censys.io/api/v2/hosts/` (Basic auth) | 250 queries/month |
Both sources skipped silently when keys aren't configured. Without any keys the tool is a no-op (returns success=True with both sources skipped).
Auto-detects target type. For domain targets, resolves up to 3 A records and queries each IP through both sources. URL-shaped input auto-stripped to hostname. Private / loopback / link-local IPs rejected.
Findings (severity tuned to attacker-impact):
- **High** (CWE-200, attack_surface_disclosure) — high-risk service exposed on public IP. Detection from product/service-name fingerprints OR well-known port mapping. Catches: SSH, Telnet, RDP, VNC, SMB, rsync, FTP, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MSSQL, MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch, Memcached, Kibana, Docker API, Kubernetes API, etcd. Per-IP dedup so a host running both ssh and telnet emits ONE high-risk-service finding listing both. - **High** (CWE-1395, vulnerable_software) — Shodan-tagged CVE on the host. One finding per CVE (capped at 20 per IP). The tracer's KEV enrichment auto-decorates these. - **Medium** (CWE-200) — broad attack surface (>10 distinct ports exposed). Signals poorly-segmented host. - **Low** (CWE-200) — service version disclosure in banners. Feeds-forward to `cve_lookup` (#61) rather than acting on directly. Aggregates all version disclosures per IP into ONE low finding.
Per-host dedup keys: `(ip, severity, class)` so each detection class emits at most one finding per IP. Per-detection verdicts still live in `result["per_ip"]` for the agent.
`verification_status=needs_review` since Shodan / Censys can carry stale data (services may have been firewalled / decommissioned since the last scan).
Cache: per-target JSON cache under `~/.strix/attack_surface_cache/`, 6-hour TTL. Stale cache served on full-source failure (fail-open with `error` populated). Disable with `STRIX_ATTACK_SURFACE_NO_CACHE=1`.
Composes with cluster-A safety: rate-limit applies to outbound HTTP requests. `--exclude-path` doesn't apply (URLs are Shodan / Censys, not the customer's domain).

parameter.name: target
parameter.description: Domain (e.g. `example.com`) or IPv4 address (e.g. `8.8.8.8`). URL-shaped input auto-stripped to hostname. Private / loopback / link-local IPs rejected.

returns.description:
{success, target, target_type, queried_at, from_cache, resolved_ips, per_ip: [{ip, shodan: {present, ports, services, vulns, last_update, ...} | {skipped, reason}, censys: {present, ports, services, last_updated, autonomous_system, ...} | {skipped, reason}, all_ports, high_risk_services: [{port, service}], broad_surface, version_disclosure: [{port, product, version}], shodan_vulns}, ...], source_errors, findings_emitted}.
The agent should: 1. Feed each `version_disclosure` entry into `cve_lookup` (#61) to find known CVEs for that (product, version). 2. Treat `high_risk_services` findings as immediate-priority (real-world breach paths). 3. Run subsequent scans (port scans, service-specific probes) against the IPs that surface in `per_ip`.
